Quick update from infra: we see a correlated increase in KV-cache evictions and GPU memory high-water events on Hosted-pool-3 starting 08:48 PST. A subset of pods observed OOM-killed kernels and falling back to CPU infer (hence the 503s/timeouts).

Initial hypothesis: an allocator/kernel change rolled this morning increased fragmentation for long-lived KV caches on models with >28B params, producing reduced contiguous GPU allocations under heavy tail load. This leads to soft OOMs and retries at the runtime layer.

Actions taken (09:22–09:32):
- Isolated affected nodes and diverted new traffic (partial routing to Hosted-pool-4).
- Enabled aggressive KV cache trimming for the heavy models to free contiguous mem quickly.
- Spun up two extra GPU workers in Hosted-pool-4 for BrightLane's region.
- Collected perf bundle and core dump: perf_traces_20261111.zip, kv_eviction_sample.log, core_dump_311.bin (attached).

We need eng to confirm rollback of the allocator tweak and consider an emergency kernel-side fix. Recommending temporary customer fallback to the 8K-context model variant that uses less KV state — lower quality but stable.

Marissa Cole
Sr Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
